candidate_relations.rationale: The checkpoint tests independently verify deterministic non-mutating construction and fail-closed handling of malformed primitive observations, strengthening the checkpoint-adapter proposition that the adapter is read-only.

The manifest schema binds content identity and transport SHA-256 as distinct fields alongside semantic package metadata, strengthening the accepted contract's separation of semantic content identity from exact transport-byte integrity.

The project-identity bridge tests verify that v2 identity is valid bootstrap state and that first admission reuses that exact identity, strengthening the project-identity amendment's first-admission project-seeding requirement.

The mutation runtime's explicit proposal revalidation and validation of proposal/approval artifacts before state transitions strengthens the adapter contracts requiring proposal applicability to be revalidated immediately before fresh direct approval.

The production-invocation tests independently verify operation without source-repository fallback and unchanged project-owned canonical bytes, strengthening the Distiller-core proposition that it has no source-repository fallback or canonical mutation path.

The narrower installer-runner contract statement that package retrieval and release selection stay outside installer execution directly strengthens the broader rd_install.py runner contract containing the same boundary.

The Rupi update/recovery tests verify recovery requires bounded intent and replanning while update reuses accepted installer mutation, strengthening the R6 amendment's shared-orchestration and fresh-transition-planning requirements.

The install-package contract tests reject malformed paths, invalid modes/digests, and incorrect content identity, strengthening the accepted install-package contract's integrity and semantic-identity requirements.
The Rupi update/recovery tests independently verify managed drift stops mutation, strengthening the installer-runner contract's fail-closed managed-drift requirement.

The production-invocation tests' byte-for-byte preservation of project-owned authority and canonical state strengthens the install-package contract boundary that project knowledge and authority remain outside the framework-managed root.
